question: How can perception remain distinct when its field is the same?
premises: Perception may operate in an equal or shared field.
The cognitions of pot and non-pot do not become the same.
Perception manifests with its own unmistakable clarity.
inference: Therefore perception expands without rival even when its field is shared.
plain_english: Even when perception operates in the same field, the cognition of a pot and of a non-pot are not identical; thus perception itself shines forth unrivaled.
